contract:
# Memory Observatory — complete local system contract v1

Build a complete working Node.js 26.8.1 system using only standard-library modules.
Deliver package.json, src/core.mjs, src/store.mjs, src/server.mjs, src/cli.mjs,
test/system.test.mjs and README.md. Additional src/*.mjs or test/*.mjs files allowed.
No external dependency, network client, external service, authentication secret,
repository import, UI framework or installed tool is available. All source is ESM.

Product: let a developer create and revise retained instructions, disable reuse,
ask which instructions apply to a request and inspect durable history. The system
is local and single-writer per store. HTTP binds only 127.0.0.1. CLI operations
run while the server for that store is stopped; concurrent independent writers
are outside this prototype. Both interfaces share behavior and persistent state.

Identity: (product_id, participant_id, lesson_id); every operation requires an
explicit product and participant. No list, explain, export or history operation
may include another scope. IDs and source_ref and instruction are nonempty strings.
Conditions/exclusions are arrays of nonempty strings, default []; duplicates may
be rejected or deduplicated. Use exact identity equality and case-insensitive
substring matching for conditions/exclusions. No semantic classifier is needed.

Store: --store is an exact JSON file path; create parent directories if needed.
Persist {schema_version:1,lessons:[...],events:[...]}. Atomic replace-on-write is
required. Each lesson stores its identity, instruction, conditions, exclusions,
source_ref, revision (starting at 1), disabled (starting false). Events are
append-only records with unique increasing integer event_id, kind (created,
revised, disabled), identity, revision, source_ref. Preserve immutable prior event
content. A completed success must survive process restart. A malformed existing
store must cause startup/CLI failure and must not be overwritten or reset.
There is no delete or enable endpoint. Disabling does not increment content
revision; revising increments revision and preserves disabled state.

HTTP launch: node src/server.mjs --store FILE --port 0
Print one JSON startup line containing {"port":ACTUAL_PORT}; use 127.0.0.1.
All responses are JSON. Errors have {"error":{"code":STRING,"message":STRING}}.
Reject malformed JSON with HTTP 400. GET unknown path -> 404. Bodies >65536 bytes
-> 413. Validation errors -> 400; missing scoped lesson -> 404; duplicate create
or expected_revision mismatch -> 409. Do not write data on failed operations.

Endpoints:
GET /health -> {ok:true,schema_version:1}
POST /lessons, body lesson fields -> 201 {lesson:RECORD}
GET /lessons?product_id=P&participant_id=U -> 200 {lessons:[...]}, sorted lesson_id
POST /lessons/ID/revise, body {product_id,participant_id,expected_revision,
instruction,source_ref,conditions?,exclusions?} -> 200 {lesson:RECORD}; omitted
conditions/exclusions preserve their prior values. expected_revision is required.
POST /lessons/ID/disable, body {product_id,participant_id,expected_revision}
-> 200 {lesson:RECORD}; repeated disable is idempotent, adding no duplicate event.
GET /history?product_id=P&participant_id=U&lesson_id=ID -> {events:[...]}
GET /export?product_id=P&participant_id=U -> {schema_version:1,product_id:P,
participant_id:U,lessons:[...],events:[...]}, scoped and deterministically ordered.
POST /explain, body {product_id,participant_id,text,invalidated_refs?,override_ids?}
-> {items:[{lesson_id,instruction,revision,source_ref}],assessments:[{lesson_id,
revision,disposition}]}. Only same-scope lessons are assessed, sorted lesson_id.
Disposition priority: disabled; inapplicable (a condition missing or an exclusion
present); unsupported (source_ref in invalidated_refs); overridden (lesson_id in
override_ids); applicable. items contains exactly applicable lessons. This is a
projection, not a mutation: invalidation/override must not persist or erase a lesson.

CLI: node src/cli.mjs --store FILE COMMAND --json JSON_OBJECT
COMMAND is create, revise, disable, list, history, export or explain. Inputs match
HTTP bodies/query fields; revise/disable/history also require lesson_id in input.
Success writes exactly one JSON result to stdout and exits 0. Failure writes one
JSON error to stderr and exits nonzero. No extra banners. State must interoperate
with server-created stores and vice versa. --help exits 0 and explains commands.

Testing/docs: model-authored tests should import core/store functions directly,
use temporary data and need no subprocesses. Tests run with node --test
--test-isolation=none. Document launch, every command, persistence, single-writer
scope, error handling and sample create/revise/explain/history workflows. Tests
and documentation are part of the delivered system. The evaluator separately
launches the real server and CLI and validates behavior, including restarts.

Resume clarification: non-object JSON bodies are validation errors (400). History for a missing scoped lesson is 404. Model tests may be invoked by direct import of node:test modules to avoid host test discovery problems.

# Product change — expiring preferences and old-store compatibility

All v1 behavior remains required, with these exact changes:
1. Current health, store and export schema_version become 2.
2. Lessons may have expires_at: null or a nonnegative safe integer UTC epoch
   milliseconds. Omitted on create defaults to null. Invalid values -> 400.
3. Revise may set expires_at; omission preserves it, explicit null clears it.
4. Explain accepts optional now, a nonnegative safe integer epoch milliseconds;
   omission uses Date.now(). A lesson expires when now >= expires_at.
5. Disposition precedence is disabled, expired, inapplicable, unsupported,
   overridden, applicable. Expired records stay inspectable and have no items.
6. Load v1 stores without losing lessons, IDs, revisions, disable controls or
   event history. Treat missing expires_at as null. Persist schema_version 2
   atomically during migration. Existing event objects must remain unchanged.
7. Reopening a migrated store must not migrate twice or duplicate history.
8. Both CLI and HTTP implement the new fields and docs/tests cover them.
Expiry is a projection decision, not automatic deletion or product authority.

# Memory Observatory v2

Memory Observatory is a local, single-writer retained-instruction store using only Node.js standard-library modules. Data is scoped by the exact `(product_id, participant_id, lesson_id)` identity. The HTTP server binds only to `127.0.0.1`.

## Launch and persistence

```sh
node src/server.mjs --store ./data/memory.json --port 0
```

The server creates parent directories and prints one startup JSON line such as `{"port":43127}`. The persistent store uses `schema_version: 2`, contains `lessons` and append-only `events`, and is written using an atomic temporary-file replacement. Successful writes survive restart. Existing v1 stores are migrated once: every lesson receives `expires_at: null`, event objects are retained, and the migrated file is persisted as schema 2. A malformed existing file causes startup or CLI failure; it is never reset or overwritten. Use one writer for a store and stop the server before using the CLI for that same file.

Lessons have `expires_at: null` or a nonnegative safe integer UTC epoch millisecond value. Create defaults it to null. Revise preserves it when omitted and clears it with explicit `null`. Expiry is a projection decision: it never deletes a lesson or event.

## HTTP API

All responses are JSON. Validation errors and malformed JSON return `400`; bodies larger than 65536 bytes return `413`; missing scoped lessons return `404`; duplicate identities and revision conflicts return `409`.

```sh
# Health
curl http://127.0.0.1:43127/health

# Create
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:43127/lessons -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"product_id":"demo","participant_id":"alice","lesson_id":"deploy","instruction":"Review the rollout","conditions":["deploy"],"source_ref":"runbook:7","expires_at":4102444800000}'

# Revise; omitted conditions, exclusions, and expires_at are preserved
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:43127/lessons/deploy/revise -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"product_id":"demo","participant_id":"alice","expected_revision":1,"instruction":"Review the staged rollout","source_ref":"runbook:8"}'

# Explain at a deterministic time; invalidation and override are request-only
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:43127/explain -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"product_id":"demo","participant_id":"alice","text":"We will deploy today","now":4102440000000,"invalidated_refs":[],"override_ids":[]}'

# List, history, and export are scope-specific
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:43127/lessons?product_id=demo&participant_id=alice'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:43127/history?product_id=demo&participant_id=alice&lesson_id=deploy'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:43127/export?product_id=demo&participant_id=alice'

# Disable; revision stays unchanged and repeated disable is idempotent
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:43127/lessons/deploy/disable -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"product_id":"demo","participant_id":"alice","expected_revision":2}'
```

`/explain` assesses all lessons in the requested scope, sorted by `lesson_id`. Disposition priority is `disabled`, `expired`, `inapplicable`, `unsupported`, `overridden`, then `applicable`. Only applicable lessons appear in `items`. Conditions and exclusions use case-insensitive substring matching. `invalidated_refs` and `override_ids` are transient projections and do not persist or erase lessons.

## CLI

The CLI uses the same store and behavior. Every command takes a JSON object and writes exactly one JSON result to stdout on success. Errors are one JSON object on stderr and have a nonzero exit status. Run it only while the server for that store is stopped.

```sh
node src/cli.mjs --store ./data/memory.json create --json '{"product_id":"demo","participant_id":"alice","lesson_id":"deploy","instruction":"Review the rollout","source_ref":"runbook:7","expires_at":4102444800000}'
node src/cli.mjs --store ./data/memory.json revise --json '{"product_id":"demo","participant_id":"alice","lesson_id":"deploy","expected_revision":1,"instruction":"Review the staged rollout","source_ref":"runbook:8","expires_at":null}'
node src/cli.mjs --store ./data/memory.json explain --json '{"product_id":"demo","participant_id":"alice","text":"deploy now","now":4102440000000}'
node src/cli.mjs --store ./data/memory.json history --json '{"product_id":"demo","participant_id":"alice","lesson_id":"deploy"}'
node src/cli.mjs --store ./data/memory.json list --json '{"product_id":"demo","participant_id":"alice"}'
node src/cli.mjs --store ./data/memory.json export --json '{"product_id":"demo","participant_id":"alice"}'
node src/cli.mjs --store ./data/memory.json disable --json '{"product_id":"demo","participant_id":"alice","lesson_id":"deploy","expected_revision":2}'
node src/cli.mjs --help
```

## Errors and scope

Every operation explicitly validates `product_id` and `participant_id`. List and export never include another scope. History requires an existing lesson in the requested exact scope. Failed validation, duplicate creation, revision conflicts, and missing lessons do not write data. Store events contain immutable identity, revision, source reference, kind, and increasing event IDs.

## Tests

Model-authored tests import `src/core.mjs` and `src/store.mjs` directly, use temporary data, cover v1 migration, expiry projection, persistence, history, scope isolation, and malformed storage, and do not spawn subprocesses:

```sh
node --test --test-isolation=none
```
